Rashi on Shabbat 90b:1:1.english: Cucumber seeds - It is significant, and [one is] liable for two seeds.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:1:2.hebrew: המוציא חגב חי כל שהוא - שמצניעין אותו לקטן לשחק בו, כדמפרש רבי יהודה בסיפא דמתני':
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:1:2.english: One who carries out a live locust [is liable for] any amount - Because they store it away for a child to play with, as Rabbi Yehuda explains at the end of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:1:3.english: Dead - It is like other foods, and [one] is liable for a dried-fig's bulk.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:1:4.english: Tzipporet keramim - Later on, [the Gemara] explains what it is and what its remedy is.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:1:5.hebrew: שמצניעים אותו לקטן כו' - ות"ק מהאי טעמא נמי מחייב ליה בחגב טהור, ומיהו אטמא פליג, דלא מצנעי ליה לשחק, דילמא אכיל ליה, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:1:5.english: Because they store it for a child, etc. - And the Tanna Kamma also holds him liable for a kosher locust for this [same] reason; however, he disagrees regarding a non-kosher [locust], because they do not store it to play [with], lest [the child] eat it, as [stated] below.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:2:1.english: To fertilize - Thus we see [that] a plant that comes from a single seed is [considered] significant.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:2:2.hebrew: הא דזריע - מאחר שהן זרועין, חשיב כל אחד ואחד, ואדם טורח לזבל אחד מהם. אבל דלא זריע, אין אדם טורח לזרוע גרגיר אחד:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:2:2.english: This [refers to where] it is [already] planted - Since they are planted, each and every one is significant, and a person bothers to fertilize one of them. But [where] it is not [yet] planted, a person does not bother to plant a single seed.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:1.english: One who carries out pits - Date pits.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:10.hebrew: תורי דקל - דקין מצורי, והן מן הסיב הגדל סביבותיו, ולא ידעתי למאי חזי:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:10.english: Palm vines - [They are] thinner than tzurei [palm shoots], and they are from the fiber that grows around it [the palm], and I do not know what it is fit for.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:2.hebrew: ביצה קלה - כגרוגרת מביצה שהיא קלה לבשל, וזו של תרנגולת:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:2.english: An easily [cooked] egg - Like a dried fig's bulk of an egg that is easy to cook, and that is [an egg] of a chicken.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:3.english: For counting - Like [what] they place as a sign of testimony for each simple dinar.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:4.hebrew: אחרים אומרים ה' - דעד ד' כללות חשיב איניש ולא מינשי, ואין צריך לתת סימן. אבל חמש, מינשי ומותיב סימנא לכולהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:4.english: Others say five - For up to four sums a person counts [in his mind] and does not forget, and does not need to set a marker; but [for] five, he forgets and sets a marker for all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:5.hebrew: לנישבין - לצוד עופות, ובלע"ז ליצ"ש:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:5.english: For traps [lenishvin] - To catch birds, and in Old French: *laz* [snares].

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:6.english: Stiff hair of a pig - Stiff hairs that are on the spine of a pig.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:7.english: One [hair] - For it is fit for cobblers to place at the tip of the sewing thread.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:3:8.english: Palm shoots - Peeled shoots [used] to make baskets.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:1.english: Paylei bayrei - This is its name.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:10.hebrew: ואי לא - אכיל ליה, אלא שדי ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:10.english: And if [he does] not - eat it, but rather throws it away.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:11.english: His learning is uprooted - And his wisdom that he learned through it is uprooted from him.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:2.hebrew: ומשתכח בדיקלא דחד נבארא - בדקל בחור, שלא נכרך עדיין אלא בסיב א' שגדל סביבותיו וכורכו:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:2.english: And it is found in a palm tree of one nevara - In a young palm tree, which has not yet been wrapped except with one fiber that grows around it and wraps it.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:3.english: For wisdom - To open the heart.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:5.hebrew: שיתין - לאו דוקא, אלא מכסהו כסויין הרבה, כגון זפת ושעוה על גבה ואדמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:5.english: Sixty - Not literally [sixty], rather he covers it [with] many coverings, such as pitch, and wax on top of it, and earth.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:7.hebrew: ותלי ליה באיברא דשמאל' - בזרוע השמאלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:7.english: And [he] hangs it on the left limb - on the left arm.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:8.english: And the mnemonic, “a fool’s heart” - [Refers to] one such as this, who needs to open [his] heart — [it is hung] on his left [arm].

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:4:9.english: And he eats the other half - After he has grown wise.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:1.hebrew: ות"ק סבר - חגב טמא לא מצנעי' ליה לקטן לשחק:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:1.english: And the first tanna holds - They do not put away a non-kosher locust for a child to play [with].

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:2.hebrew: דילמא אכיל - ואפי' למאן דאמר קטן אוכל נבלות אין ב"ד מצויין עליו להפרישו, מודה הוא דלא יהבינן ליה בידים, דתניא (יבמות דף קד.): לא תאכלום — לא תאכילום, להזהיר גדולים על הקטנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:2.english: Perhaps he will eat [it] - And even according to the one who says [that when] a minor eats neveilot [non-kosher meat], the court is not commanded regarding him to separate him [from it], he agrees that we do not give [it] to him directly, as it is taught in a baraita (Yevamot 104a): "You shall not eat them" [also means] "You shall not feed them," to warn adults regarding minors.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:3.hebrew: אי הכי טהור - חי נמי, דילמא אכיל ליה. ואי משום דאין בו איסור אבר מן החי, דחגב אין טעון שחיטה, אית ביה מיהא משום בל תשקצו, במסכת מכות (דף טז:) כדרב כהנא כו':
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:3.english: If so, a kosher [locust] - [when] alive as well, perhaps he will eat it. And if [you say it is permitted] because there is no prohibition of a limb from a living [creature] with it, since a locust does not require ritual slaughter, nevertheless it involves [a violation] on account of "You shall not make yourselves detestable," [as stated] in Tractate Makkot (16b), as [in the incident] of Rav Kahana, etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:4.english: Shushiva - A species of kosher locust.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:5.hebrew: אלא - לאו משום דחייש דילמא אכיל לי' חי, אלא דילמא מיית ואכיל לי', וקאכיל טמא; אבל טהור ש"ד:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:5.english: Rather - [it is] not because he is concerned lest [the child] eat it alive, rather lest it die and he eat it, and [thereby] eat a non-kosher [locust]; whereas a kosher [one] is fine.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:6.hebrew: מיספד ספיד ליה - תינוק, ולאו אורחיה למיכליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:5:6.english: He will eulogize it - A child [will eulogize it], and it is not his way to eat it.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:7:1.english: One who stores [is liable for] any amount - For he deemed it significant.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:7:2.hebrew: אלא כשיעורו - בכל אחד שיעור המפורש לו: בזרעונין חמשה, זרע קישואין או דילועין או פול המצרי שנים, ובשאר ובשאר דברים — כגון יין או אוכלין או גני — כשיעור המפורש בכלל גדול ובהמוציא:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:7:2.english: Only according to its measure - For each [item, there is] the measure that is specified for it: for garden seeds, five; for cucumber seeds, or gourd seeds, or Egyptian bean [seeds], two; and for other things — such as wine, or foods, or reeds [גני] — according to the measure that is specified in [the chapters] Kelal Gadol and HaMotzi.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:7:3.hebrew: חזר והכניסו - זה שהצניע פחות מכשיעור והוציאו, אם חזר ונמלך שלא לזורעו והכניסו:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:7:3.english: [If] he went back and brought it in - [This refers to] the one who stored away less than the [prescribed] measure and carried it out: if he reconsidered, [deciding] not to sow it, and brought it [back] in.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:7:4.hebrew: אינו חייב - בהכנסה זו אלא אם כן יש בו שיעור שלם, דכיון דנמלך עליו שלא לזורעו, ביטל מחשבתו, והרי הוא ככל אדם:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:7:4.english: He is not liable - for this bringing [it] in unless it contains a full measure, for since he changed his mind about it, not to sow it, he nullified his [original] intention, and he is like any [other] person.

Rashi on Shabbat 90b:8:1.hebrew: ליתני המוציא זרע בכל שהוא חייב - ואף על גב דלא אצנעיה מעיקרא להכי, דהא דבעינן שיעורא, היינו טעמא כדאמרן, שאין אדם טורח להוציא נימא אחת לזריעה. הלכך, מוציא סתם פטור עד שיהא בו שיעור. אבל זה שהוציא נימא אחת לזריעה בהדיא, גלי דעתיה דטרח ואחשביה:
Rashi on Shabbat 90b:8:1.english: Let [the Mishnah] teach: One who carries out seed of any amount is liable - Even though he did not store it originally for this [purpose]. For [the reason] that we require a [minimum] measure is the reason as we said [earlier]: that a person does not bother to carry out a single tiny bit for planting. Therefore, one who carries out [something] without a specific purpose is exempt unless it has the [minimum] measure. However, this [person], who carried out a single tiny bit explicitly for planting, has revealed his intent that he bothered [over it] and deemed it significant.

Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:1:1.hebrew: שמצניעין אותו לחזיר - פירוש: שראוי ליתן לעובד כוכבים או למכור לו, אבל ישראל אסור לגדל חזיר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:1:1.english: For they store it for a pig - Explanation: it is fit to give to a non-Jew or to sell to him, but a Jew is forbidden to raise a pig.

Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:3:1.hebrew: אם לנטיעה שתים - פי' אותם שהם ראויים לנטיעה, אי נמי כלומר במקום שרגילין לנוטען והוי סתמא לנטוע; דאי במוציא ממש לנטיעה, הא אמר בריש פ' המצניע (לקמן שבת צא.): מחייב היה ר' מאיר במוציא חטה א' לזריעה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:3:1.english: "If [he carried them out] to plant — two" - This means those [pits] that are fit for planting; or alternatively, [it] means in a place where people are accustomed to plant them, and an unspecified [carrying out] is [considered] for planting. For if [it were speaking] of one who actually carries [them] out to plant, did [the Gemara] not say at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] HaMatzni'a (below, Shabbat 91a): Rabbi Meir held [one] liable for carrying out one wheat kernel for sowing?

Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:5:1.hebrew: דלא לימרו מיכל קא אכיל ליה ועבר משום בל תשקצו - אומר רשב"א דמשמע מכאן דחגב טהור אין טעון שחיטה, מדלא קאמר דלא לימרו דקאכיל ליה בלא שחיטה. ועוד, דת"ק קאמר בסמוך בחגב חי טמא: "דילמא מיית ואכיל ליה", ובטהור לא חייש; והיינו משום דמותר בלא שחיטה. ובתוספתא דמסכת תרומות תניא: "אוכל אדם חגבים בין חיין בין שחוטין". ואע"ג דאסור לאכול חי משום "בל תשקצו", מ"מ מותר לחתוך ממנו אבר ולאוכלו על ידי רחיצה, ואין בו משום אבר מן החי. ורש"י הביאו באלו טרפות (חולין דף סו.) מה"ג, דמפיק חגבים אין טעונין שחיטה מדכתיב: "ואת כל נפש החיה הרומשת במים" — אלו דגים, "ואת כל נפש השורצת" — אלו חגבים; מדכתיב חגבים אחר דגים, משמע דאין טעונין שחיטה כדגים. ואפילו עוף הוה פטרינן ליה בולא כלום, אי לאו דהוקש לבהמה, כדאמר בהשוחט (שם כז:):
Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:5:1.english: "So that [people] will not say: He is eating it and violating 'You shall not make yourselves detestable'" - Rashba says that it is implied from here that a kosher locust does not require ritual slaughter, since [Rav] did not say, "so that [people] will not say that he is eating it without ritual slaughter." Furthermore, the first tanna says immediately below regarding a live non-kosher locust, "perhaps it will die and he will eat it," whereas regarding a kosher [locust] he is not concerned; and this is because it is permitted without ritual slaughter. And in the Tosefta of Tractate Terumot it is taught: "A person may eat locusts whether [they are] alive or slaughtered." And even though it is forbidden to eat [a locust] alive because of [the prohibition] "You shall not make yourselves detestable," nevertheless it is permitted to cut a limb from it and eat it by means of washing, and it is not subject to [the prohibition of] a limb from a living creature. And Rashi cited it in [the chapter] Eilu Tereifot (Chullin 66a) from Halakhot Gedolot, which derives [that] locusts do not require ritual slaughter from what is written: "And every living creature that moves in the water" — these are fish; "and every swarming creature" — these are locusts; since locusts are written after fish, it is implied that they do not require ritual slaughter, just like fish. And even a bird we would have exempted with nothing at all [i.e., without ritual slaughter], were it not that it was juxtaposed [in Scripture] to an animal, as [the Gemara] states in [the chapter] Hashochet (ibid. 27b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:5:2.hebrew: ועובר משום בל תשקצו - משמע דשושיבא שרי. ואומר ר"ת דבפ"ב דמס' ע"ז (דך לז.), גבי "איל קמצא" דמפרש רב פפא דהיינו שושיבא, ורב חייא בר אשי אמר משמיה דעולא "סוסבל", וקאמר התם "דבראשו ארוך היינו שושיבא כ"ע לא פליגי דאסור" — ל"ג "דאסור", אלא גרס "כ"ע לא פליגי דשרי"; דהכא משמע דשושיבא שרי ולית ביה אלא משום "בל תשקצו", וסתם מתניתין דפרק אלו טריפות (חולין דף סה:) שרי ראשו ארוך. לכך נראה לר"ת דגרס "כ"ע לא פליגי דשרי":
Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:5:2.english: And violating "You shall not make yourselves detestable" - [This] implies that shushiva [a type of locust] is permitted. And Rabbeinu Tam says that in the second chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (37a), regarding ayil kamtza, where Rav Pappa explains that it is shushiva and Rav Chiya bar Ashi said in the name of Ulla [that it is] susbal, and it says there: "Regarding [a locust] whose head is long, which is shushiva, everyone agrees that it is forbidden" — we do not read "that it is forbidden"; rather, read "everyone agrees that it is permitted." For here it implies that shushiva is permitted and there is no [prohibition] in it except because of "You shall not make yourselves detestable," and the unattributed Mishnah in the chapter Eilu Tereifot (Chullin 65b) permits [a locust] whose head is long. Therefore, it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that we read "everyone agrees that it is permitted."

Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:7:1.hebrew: המצניע וכל אדם אין חייבין עליו אלא כשיעורו - תימה לר"י, דאמאי איצטריך למיתני ליה? הא תנא ליה חדא זימנא בפרק כלל גדול (לעיל שבת דף עה:): "ושאינו כשר להצניע אינו חייב אלא המצניע":
Tosafot on Shabbat 90b:7:1.english: One who stores [for sowing, etc.], and any [other] person is only liable for it if [he carries out] its measure - It is surprising to the Ri [Rabbi Yitzchak]: why was it necessary to teach this, when [the Tanna] already taught it once in the chapter [entitled] Kelal Gadol (above, Shabbat 75b): "and [for] that which is not fit to store, only the one who stores it is liable"?
